summary: Three fixes verified; claim locking still permits a lost update when the improvements directory is symlinked.

findings.summary: Claim and add acquire different locks when the improvements directory is a symlink.
findings.evidence: ENG-23 and ENG-26: add passes the unresolved <home>/improvements path to lock.acquire, which uses <home>/improvements.lock.json. Claim resolves the directory first and locks beside the symlink target instead. With a symlinked improvements directory, add can scan a ready entry while claim changes it to claimed, then replace it with ready again, reproducing the lost-claim defect.
findings.fix: Use the same canonical lock identity for both operations, or reject symlinked backlog directories consistently; add a CLI regression test covering the symlinked case.

findings.summary: The lock serialization test relies on subprocess scheduling instead of proving claim reached the lock.
findings.evidence: ENG-18: after launching claim, the test sleeps for 0.3 seconds and checks only that the process is alive. On a loaded host, claim may not have reached its lock attempt before the parent releases the lock, so an implementation that does not wait can pass; the three-second completion timeout can also fail under scheduling delays.
findings.fix: Synchronize with the child at its lock attempt using deterministic process coordination, then assert that it cannot complete until the held lock is released.
